mechanism_narrative: The significant and sustained decline in PARKS mobility, especially in the most recent week, indicates the onset of colder weather, which will reduce general outdoor activity and consequently depress retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite PARKS mobility remaining at or below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high residential mobility, particularly if it remains above 9% for two consecutive weeks, signals a continued preference for staying home, which directly reduces out-of-home discretionary spending and drives down retail and recreation mobility.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 9% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, even as RESIDENTIAL mobility consistently remains above 9%.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stagnation and slight decline in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a plateau in the return-to-office trend, which will continue to suppress weekday foot traffic and negatively impact retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility remaining stagnant or declining.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains relatively stable (above -7%) while RETAIL_REC continues its recent decline (below -20%), it indicates a shift in consumer priorities towards essential spending, further depressing discretionary retail over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -7% while RETAIL_REC falls below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, even as GROCERY_PHARM remains stable and RETAIL_REC initially declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility, possibly due to a temporary spell of milder weather, could lead to a short-term rebound in outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The broad decline observed across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES in the most recent week signifies a general suppression of out-of-home activity, which will continue to exert downward pressure on retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: A majority of the listed mobility categories show a sustained increase over the next 28 days, yet RETAIL_REC continues to fall.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility shows a sustained increase of more than 2 points week-on-week and remains above -18%, it indicates a renewed push for office returns, which will generate increased foot traffic and positively impact retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 2 points week-on-week and stays above -18%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility shows a sustained increase as described, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent trend of increasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and decreasing RETAIL_REC mobility suggests a reinforcing cycle of people staying home and reducing discretionary outings, which will continue to depress retail activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases while RETAIL_REC decreases week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases and RETAIL_REC also increases over the next 28 days, contradicting the inverse relationship.
